Colorful leaves (紅葉, kōyō) are to the Japanese autumn what [cherry blossoms](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2011.html) are to spring. The viewing of autumn leaves has been a popular activity in Japan for centuries and today draws large numbers of travelers to famous koyo spots both in the mountains and in the cities.

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g17/2014_map.png)

Each year, starting in mid September, the "koyo front" slowly moves southwards from the northern island of [Hokkaido](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1101.html) until it reaches the lower elevations of central and southern Japan around late November. Some trees around [Tokyo](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2164.html) and [Kyoto](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2158.html) remain colorful into December.

# Best Hokkaido Fall Foliage Spots

9/12/2025

[Hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/usa/en-us/taxonomy/term/1/)

[Autumn](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/usa/en-us/taxonomy/term/116/)

[Nature](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/usa/en-us/taxonomy/term/166/)

[Sightseeing spots/Famous destinations](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/usa/en-us/taxonomy/term/96/)

As Japan’s northernmost island, [Hokkaido](https://maps.app.goo.gl/CpdK3vYECvQzKTz98) is the first place in the country to welcome the autumn’s vibrant hues. Beginning as early as mid-September, the mountains, lakes, and highlands of Hokkaido erupt into fiery shades of red, gold, and amber – weeks ahead of the rest of Japan.

Known locally as _koyo_, the changing leaves are celebrated much like cherry blossoms in spring. Travelers flock to mountainsides and hot springs to admire the fleeting beauty of autumn and soak in the crisp, cool air. And because of Hokkaido’s varied elevations and cooler climate, the season rolls out in stages – offering visitors multiple chances to catch the colors in full.

If you’ve never experienced autumn in Japan before, Hokkaido is the perfect place to start. Here’s your seasonal guide to Hokkaido’s early fall foliage – from when and where to go, to how to make the most of your visit.

## Best time to visit Hokkaido for fall foliage

Image

![early-fall-foliage-hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/sites/contents/files/styles/max_1300x1300/public/2025-09/early-fall-foliage-hokkaido_3.jpg?itok=B5yJyBlE)

While most of Japan sees autumn colors in late October and November, Hokkaido’s high elevation areas begin changing as early as mid-September. In fact, the very first hints of red commonly appear in [Daisetsuzan National Park](https://maps.app.goo.gl/fCHpzUYvgNde1xh2A) around September 15th – making it the earliest koyo destination in the country.

The season gradually moves downward from the mountaintops to lower valleys and towns. This staggered timing means you can chase the colors from one area to the next depending on your travel dates.

For reference, here’s the progression:

**Mid to Late September:**

**・Daisetsuzan National Park (Asahidake, Kurodake)**: This is the first place in Japan where leaves begin to turn. Visit around mid-September for views of fiery reds and folds against alpine peaks.

**・** [**Shiretoko**](https://maps.app.goo.gl/vmzb9Z6puryWcmMe8) **and** [**Lake Akan**](https://maps.app.goo.gl/gefE2Tu7ExtpHLBY7): These eastern Hokkaido destinations start showing color slightly later in the month. Both are known for untouched nature, with forests and crater lakes that glow in amber tones.

**Early to Mid-October:**

**・Daisetsuzan National Park**: continues its transition into lower elevation areas.

**・** [**Noboribetsu**](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/usa/en-us/guide/noboribetsu-onsen-guide/) **and** [**Jozankei**](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/usa/en-us/guide/jozankei-onsen-guide/): Here, the leaves begin to turn by early October, offering beautiful riverside foliage and easy access from [Sapporo](https://maps.app.goo.gl/cgj4xq8guK9Kbf7N7).

**・** [**Shikotsuko**](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/usa/en-us/guide/lake-shikotsu/) **(Lake Shikotsu)**: Best viewed in mid-October, this caldera laker is surrounded by vibrant forests that reflect stunningly on its glassy surface

**Late October:**

**・Jozankei**: reaches peak color and is a great choice for late October visitors seeking vibrant foliage with the convenience of a hot spring town.

**・** [**Onuma Park**](https://maps.app.goo.gl/cNu7HQxq51KyuU2r6): Just north of [Hakodate](https://maps.app.goo.gl/cB8sSqWy2v7XgskN7), this park also begins to peak around this time. Its small islands and lakes are framed by autumn trees, making it a peaceful end to the early foliage season.

This predictable cascade of color makes Hokkaido ideal for koyo chasers, allowing you to plan a sequential route to follow the foliage from mountain tops down to city outskirts.

[See hotels in Hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/usa/en-us/explorer/cnt_japan/sub_hokkaido/?searchText=link)

## Where to see fall foliage in Hokkaido

### 1.   Daisetsuzan National Park (Asahidake, Kurodake)

Image

![fall-foliage-hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/sites/contents/files/styles/max_1300x1300/public/2024-09/fall-foliage-hokkaido_8.jpg?itok=Gbknt9OC)

Image

![fall-foliage-hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/sites/contents/files/styles/max_1300x1300/public/2024-09/fall-foliage-hokkaido_13.jpg?itok=gk1hFTp9)

**Peak Foliage**: Mid-September

As Japan’s earliest koyo destination, Daisetsuzan National Park is a dream for early autumn seekers. This vast, mountainous park in central Hokkaido is known for its rugged alpine scenery and dramatic seasonal contrasts. The two most popular areas for fall foliage are [Asahidake](https://maps.app.goo.gl/RnL7piVTZLhf6PSZ6) and [Kurodake](https://maps.app.goo.gl/y2myrGTYGraQqhax6), both offering ropeway access to high elevations where fiery reds and oranges begin appearing around mid-September.

Image

![early-fall-foliage-hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/sites/contents/files/styles/max_1300x1300/public/2025-09/early-fall-foliage-hokkaido_8.jpg?itok=XyKmvMc0)

Asahidake, Hokkaido’s tallest peak, offers an ethereal mix of volcanic landscapes, steaming fumaroles, bright alpine shrubs, and an _onsen_ (hot spring) town at its base. Kurodake, on the other side of the park, is famous for its panoramic views and accessible trails. The vivid colors typically start at the summits and work their way down by early October, creating a tiered, layered effect across the park’s valleys and ridges.

[See accommodations near Asahidake Ropeway](https://travel.rakuten.com/usa/en-us/hotel_list/cnt_japan/sub_hokkaido/cty_higashikawa_town/poi_621438/?searchText=link)

### 2\.   Shiretoko Peninsula

Image

![early-fall-foliage-hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/sites/contents/files/styles/max_1300x1300/public/2025-09/early-fall-foliage-hokkaido_12.jpg?itok=sGiDQioN)

**Peak Foliage**: Late September – Early October

Located on the eastern edge of Hokkaido, the Shiretoko Peninsula is a UNESCO World Heritage Site famed for its untouched wilderness and steep forested cliffs. Autumn arrives here in late-September, painting the dense forests in deep gold and copper hues.

Image

![early-fall-foliage-hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/sites/contents/files/styles/max_1300x1300/public/2025-09/early-fall-foliage-hokkaido_11.jpg?itok=lrVDdS5R)

The best places for viewing include the [Shiretoko Five Lakes](https://maps.app.goo.gl/EprmkwrEUDezBx8r6), where wooden boardwalks take you through mirrored lake reflections surrounded by colorful foliage. Wildlife sightings – like deer or foxes – are common and add to the region's remote, natural charm.

[See accommodations near Shiretoko Peninsula](https://travel.rakuten.com/usa/en-us/hotel_list/cnt_japan/sub_hokkaido/hsp_shiretoko_hot_spring/?searchText=link)

### 3\.   Lake Akan

Image

![early-fall-foliage-hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/sites/contents/files/styles/max_1300x1300/public/2025-09/early-fall-foliage-hokkaido_5.jpg?itok=TUreJixK)

Image

![early-fall-foliage-hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/sites/contents/files/styles/max_1300x1300/public/2025-09/early-fall-foliage-hokkaido_13.jpg?itok=OyfVed14)

**Peak Foliage**: Late September–Early October

A little west of Shiretoko, Lake Akan offers a softer, more serene fall foliage experience. This crater lake is ringed by quiet forests and home to Japan’s famous _marimo_ (a cute spherical green algae), but during fall, the highlight becomes the various trees that surround the lake in crimson amber.

The [Akan Lakeside Eco Museum Center](https://maps.app.goo.gl/of12aiQEVbyT9iW19) offers walking trails and cultural exhibits, while lake cruises provide a peaceful way to view the foliage from the water.

[See accommodations near Lake Akan](https://travel.rakuten.com/usa/en-us/hotel_list/cnt_japan/sub_hokkaido/cty_kushiro_city/poi_620382/?searchText=link)

### 4\.   Noboribetsu Onsen

Image

![fall-foliage-hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/sites/contents/files/styles/max_1300x1300/public/2024-09/fall-foliage-hokkaido_10.jpg?itok=gTC_Jn_S)

Image

![fall-foliage-hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/sites/contents/files/styles/max_1300x1300/public/2024-09/fall-foliage-hokkaido_9.jpg?itok=qaFfnxzv)

**Peak Foliage:** Early October–Mid-October

Famous for its bubbling volcanic hell valley ( [_Jigokudani_](https://maps.app.goo.gl/Zb3coNQoTCobEz9h8)) and therapeutic hot spring baths, [Noboribetsu](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/usa/en-us/guide/noboribetsu-onsen-guide/) offers a unique contrast of fall colors against steam and sulfur. By early October, the surrounding forests begin to glow with warm autumn tones.

Image

![early-fall-foliage-hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/sites/contents/files/styles/max_1300x1300/public/2025-09/early-fall-foliage-hokkaido_14.jpg?itok=_bCRmv-r)

One of the best spots is the [Oyunuma River Natural Footbaths](https://maps.app.goo.gl/ELTxoyZwVfwFonrg6), where you can soak your feet in a warm geothermic stream while surrounded by golden foliage. It’s also an easy side trip from Sapporo, making it a convenient stop in any Hokkaido itinerary.

[Best Ryokans in Noboribetsu](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/usa/en-us/guide/ryokan-noboribetsu/)

[See accommodations in Noboribetsu Onsen](https://travel.rakuten.com/usa/en-us/hotel_list/cnt_japan/sub_hokkaido/hsp_noboribetsu_hot_spring/?searchText=link)

### 5\.   Lake Toya

Image

![fall-foliage-hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/sites/contents/files/styles/max_1300x1300/public/2024-09/fall-foliage-hokkaido_12.jpg?itok=p4JtnQCW)

Image

![fall-foliage-hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/sites/contents/files/styles/max_1300x1300/public/2024-09/fall-foliage-hokkaido_6.jpg?itok=woNB8RrD)

**Peak Foliage:** Early October–Late October

[Lake Toya](https://maps.app.goo.gl/oQD6NzuMVFUetyUk6) is a caldera lake in southwestern Hokkaido which is surrounded by forested hills that turn brilliant shades of red and gold in autumn. The lake’s islands and the nearby [Mount Usu](https://maps.app.goo.gl/kG7Uc4h6KWmJuaE38) provides additional vantage points for admiring the fall colors reflected in the calm waters.

[See Accommodations near Lake Toya](https://travel.rakuten.com/usa/en-us/hotel_list/cnt_japan/sub_hokkaido/cty_sobetsu_town/poi_622045/?searchText=link)

### 6\.   Jozankei Onsen

Image

![early-fall-foliage-hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/sites/contents/files/styles/max_1300x1300/public/2025-09/early-fall-foliage-hokkaido_1.jpg?itok=LBaHnzc8)

**Peak Foliage**: Mid-October–Late October

Located just an hour outside Sapporo, [Jozankei Onsen](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/usa/en-us/guide/jozankei-onsen-guide/) is one of the most accessible places to experience fall foliage in Hokkaido. Nestled in a forested valley along the [Toyohira River](https://maps.app.goo.gl/CgUNXRBZPikLarX56), it’s known for its vibrant red maples and yellow ginkgo trees that line the water’s edge.

Image

![early-fall-foliage-hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/sites/contents/files/styles/max_1300x1300/public/2025-09/early-fall-foliage-hokkaido_7.jpg?itok=lX2hNiO_)

Top viewing spots include the [Futamitsuri Bridge](https://maps.app.goo.gl/LFKdvVu8WboRGqMV7) and [Hoheikyo Dam](https://maps.app.goo.gl/rVK9rUZg3kdfbRGZA), where trees burst into color along steep canyon walls. A soak in one of the many riverside open-air baths is the perfect way to take in the scenery while staying warm.

[10 Best Hotels in Jozankei](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/usa/en-us/guide/hotels-jozankei/)

[See accommodations in Jozankei Onsen](https://travel.rakuten.com/usa/en-us/hotel_list/cnt_japan/sub_hokkaido/hsp_jozankei_hot_spring/?searchText=link)

### 7\.   Lake Shikotsu

Image

![early-fall-foliage-hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/sites/contents/files/styles/max_1300x1300/public/2025-09/early-fall-foliage-hokkaido_10.jpg?itok=3CCRJa84)

**Peak Foliage**: Mid-October–Late October

Set within [Shikotsu-Toya National Park](https://maps.app.goo.gl/GRR7DyLVGtHxHbCD9), [Lake Shikotsu](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/usa/en-us/guide/lake-shikotsu/) is a caldera lake renowned for its exceptional clarity – one of the clearest in Japan. The surrounding forests begin their autumn transformation in mid-October, with rich tones that reflect off the lake’s glassy surface.

Image

![early-fall-foliage-hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/sites/contents/files/styles/max_1300x1300/public/2025-09/early-fall-foliage-hokkaido_6.jpg?itok=nx69QeTm)

Take a walk along the lakeside promenade, or simply enjoy the view from one of the nearby cafes. The stillness of the lake combined with the crisp air and mountain colors makes for a serene early-fall experience.

[See accommodations near Lake Shikotsu](https://travel.rakuten.com/usa/en-us/hotel_list/cnt_japan/sub_hokkaido/cty_chitose_city/poi_619610/?searchText=link)

### 8\.   Onuma Park

Image

![early-fall-foliage-hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/sites/contents/files/styles/max_1300x1300/public/2025-09/early-fall-foliage-hokkaido_9.jpg?itok=3IZJyXoN)

**Peak Foliage**: Mid-October–Early November

Toward the southern tip of Hokkaido near Hakodate, Onuma Quasi-National Park feels like a quiet, miniature version of [Nikko](https://maps.app.goo.gl/hqceE76NMZoB2CCHA). With small lakes dotted by islands and footbridges, this park becomes a canvas of fall colors by late October.

Image

![early-fall-foliage-hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/sites/contents/files/styles/max_1300x1300/public/2025-09/early-fall-foliage-hokkaido_15.jpg?itok=Ut0t1ib5)

Take a boat cruise across the water, rent a bike and circle the shoreline, or walk one of the short nature trails linking islets framed by golden maples. The nearby mountains provide a dramatic backdrop, especially when dusted with early snow.

[See accommodations near Onuma Park](https://travel.rakuten.com/usa/en-us/hotel_list/cnt_japan/sub_hokkaido/cty_nanae_town/poi_618896/?searchText=link)

### 9\.   Hokkaido University Ginkgo Avenue

Image

![fall-foliage-hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/sites/contents/files/styles/max_1300x1300/public/2024-09/fall-foliage-hokkaido_4.jpg?itok=-ZcGcUn2)

Image

![fall-foliage-hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/sites/contents/files/styles/max_1300x1300/public/2024-09/fall-foliage-hokkaido_14.jpg?itok=kyko4qoD)

**Peak Foliage:** Late October–Early November

In the heart of Sapporo, [Hokkaido University Ginkgo Avenue](https://maps.app.goo.gl/Avp3vc7hbvFJK2jg6) is a 1,246 feet (380 meters)-long avenue lined with ginkgo trees offering an accessible urban autumn experience. In late-October to early November, the trees turn a vibrant yellow, creating a golden canopy over the street.

[See hotels near Hokkaido University](https://travel.rakuten.com/usa/en-us/hotel_list/cnt_japan/sub_hokkaido/cty_sapporo_city/poi_313688/?searchText=link)

## Getting to Hokkaido

Image

![fall-foliage-hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/sites/contents/files/styles/max_1300x1300/public/2024-09/fall-foliage-hokkaido_11.jpg?itok=mXaqi2Y-)

Hokkaido’s main gateway is [New Chitose Airport](https://maps.app.goo.gl/Q7Ga77nsMwU2VbkC8), located near Sapporo. The island is connected to Tokyo and other major Japanese cities by frequent flights, making it easily accessible for domestic and international travelers. An extensive network of trains, buses, and rental car services allows airport visitors to reach various fall foliage spots across the island.

[Getting from Tokyo to Hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/usa/en-us/guide/tokyo-to-hokkaido/)

## Where to stay: Akan Yuku no Sato Tsuruga

Image

![fall-foliage-hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/sites/contents/files/styles/max_1300x1300/public/2024-09/fall-foliage-hokkaido_1.jpg?itok=RLwBwjBv)

For those looking to further themselves in Hokkaido’s autumn beauty, look no further than [Akan Yuku no Sato Tsuruga](https://travel.rakuten.com/usa/en-us/hotel_info_item/cnt_japan/sub_hokkaido/cty_kushiro_city/10123456795196/?searchText=link). Located on the shores of [Lake Akan](https://maps.app.goo.gl/Kq24obELnw5NpMn9A) in eastern Hokkaido, this resort hotel provides stunning views of the surrounding fall foliage reflected in the lake's calm waters, right from your bedroom window.

Image

![fall-foliage-hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/sites/contents/files/styles/max_1300x1300/public/2024-09/fall-foliage-hokkaido_2.jpg?itok=nhtx78ZA)

Image

![fall-foliage-hokkaido](https://travel.rakuten.com/contents/sites/contents/files/styles/max_1300x1300/public/2024-09/fall-foliage-hokkaido_3.jpg?itok=TDb26fNQ)

The hotel features a choice between Western or Japanese-styled rooms, many with panoramic views of Lake Akan and the colorful Akan-Mashu National Park. The outdoor onsen baths are a particular highlight, allowing guests to soak in the mineral-rich waters while enjoying the vibrant autumn scenery.

The hotel is close to the [Ainu Kotan](https://maps.app.goo.gl/cRtLJHqAYBbJmQ3A9) for those interested in the local culture. In this village, you can learn about the indigenous Ainu people in Hokkaido and purchase traditional hand-made crafts, a unique souvenir to remember your Hokkaido adventure.

[Check room availability at Akan Yuku no Sato Tsuruga](https://travel.rakuten.com/usa/en-us/hotel_info_item/cnt_japan/sub_hokkaido/cty_kushiro_city/10123456795196/?searchText=link)

# Autumn Leaves Forecast 2025

Discover Japan during the beautiful season of autumn leaves
Toyama

Surrounded by rich nature, Japan has four magical seasons. Autumn is considered one of the most beautiful as the landscape turns vibrant shades of orange, yellow, and red. Colorful autumn leaves, known as koyo, have been admired in Japan for centuries and today, together with the Sakura (cherry blossoms), attract a large number of visitors, both local and international. The perfect time to visit these incredible sights is from late September to early December, depending on the place, elevation, and temperature of the year

Each year, the season of scenic autumn leaves begins in colder areas of northern Hokkaido and gradually moves southward to central and southern Japan. In each region, the mountains are colored first, then scenes of colored leaves spread into city gardens, parks, and temples. Both areas are definitely worth a visit.

The secret behind the picturesque vivid foliage lies in Japan’s typical autumn weather – a difference in temperature between cooler mornings, warm sunny daytime, and cold evenings that allow autumn leaves to change.

The scenic autumn season is the time of year when it is neither too hot nor too cold, making it easy and comfortable to travel. This is also the season of harvest and fine seasonal food, which potentially makes autumn the best time for you to visit.

Autumn leaves – each destination has its own unique character and beauty, including the magnificent landscapes of Hokkaido, the eye-catching color contrast of temples and trees in Kyoto, and radiant mountains across Kyushu. ​Daisetsuzan National Park is the first place in Japan where autumn descends and the brilliant changing colors of the leaves appear. From late-September to mid-October, the middle to upper elevations dazzle with reds, oranges and yellows lavished across the landscapes. Whether you're interested in a few hours' easy hiking course or a multi-day trek, we offer exceptional guiding service and an intimate knowledge of the mountains. 
Hiking at Daisetsuzan National Park can include riding ropeways, waterfall viewing, wild hot springs, fumaroles, steep ascents, descent-only trails or flat walks, peaks, mountain hut stays, camping, rivers, marshes and primary forests. Whatever your preferences, contact us to build an awesome hiking & trekking tour at Daisetsuzan National Park, or to include a shorter visit on a wider Hokkaido tour.
For those interested in exploring the region on foot, check-out our [Fall Hiking & Trekking page](https://www.hokkaidonaturetours.com/hnt-hokkaido-activities-fall-hiking-trekking.html) for full listings. |

The fall season comes early to Daisetsuzan, with many trees and shrubs turning color in late September, a few weeks ahead of other areas in Hokkaido. It's a great time to ride a ropeway up to a viewing point, walk along highland plateaus, or sneak a hike up a peak before the snow arrives in October. 
​
Popular fall activities include riding ropeways, waterfall viewing, hiking, sightseeing and hot springs. Top places to visit include Tokachidake Onsen Resort, Asahidake Onsen Resort, Sounkyo Gorge, Ginsendai and Shikaribetsu Lake. We highly recommend making Daisetsuzan National Park a part of your tour to Hokkaido.

Hiking at Daisetsuzan National Park can include riding ropeways, waterfall viewing, wild hot springs, fumaroles, steep ascents, descent-only trails or flat walks, peaks, mountain hut stays, camping, rivers, marshes and primary forests. he two main resorts at Daisetsuzan National Park - Asahidake Resort and Kurodake Resort - both have ropeways that carry visitors midway up the rugged mountain range for beautiful nature and spectacular views. Asahidake Ropeway brings passengers to the Sugatami Highland Plateau, a flat walking area with trails that meander between ponds, fumaroles and high-mountain flora. Fall is a great season for day trips to this stunning plateau, when alpine shrubs turn brilliant colors and dominate the beauty of the landscape. You may even experience some early season snow if you're lucky. The Kurodake Ropeway at Sounkyo Gorge is similarly spectacular, with views of the towering gorge and plains beyond. Large numbers of deciduous trees here create a carpet of yellow in early-October that is simply magical. | | | | | --- | --- | | [![Picture](https://www.hokkaidonaturetours.com/uploads/5/9/6/6/59665553/nakayamadake-wild-onsen_orig.jpg)](https://www.hokkaidonaturetours.com/hnt-private-custom-made-tours-preferences-form.html) | ## Hot Spring Resorts
There are three main hot spring resorts in Daisetsuzan National Park: Asahidake Resort, Sounkyo Gorge & Tokachidake Resort. There are also a few smaller hot spring areas such as at Tenninkyo, Shikaribetsu and Shirogane. With the variety of baths and spring types on offer, a hot spring bath is a must for trips to Daisetsuzan. 
There are also a number of "wild" hot springs scattered around the park that are just as wonderful to visit. You can take a foot bath or jump right in, but be aware that these "wild" _onsen_ are not for the timid. Most are mixed-baths, have little to no infrastructure or changing rooms, and are open for all to see. | | | | | --- | --- | | [![Picture](https://www.hokkaidonaturetours.com/uploads/5/9/6/6/59665553/sounkyo-fall-foliage-waterfalls_orig.jpg)](https://www.hokkaidonaturetours.com/hnt-private-custom-made-tours-preferences-form.html) | ## Waterfalls
With the massive size of Daisetsuzan National Park, it comes as no surprise that there are many large and small waterfalls to be explored. The densest cluster of falls are at Sounkyo Gorge's 8 Waterfalls Trail, where a 3 kilometer walking trail skirts the deepest part of the gorge in spectacular fashion. The fall foliage in the gorge in mid-October is one of the most stunning fall sites in Hokkaido. Asahidake Resort also has a number of small falls within easy hiking distance to the bottom of the ropeway. Further south, the Shirahige Falls, whose waters spill into the blue Biei River, are a local favorite. 
Unfortunately, the highest waterfall in Hokkaido, and one of the most beautiful, the so-called Angel's Robes Falls in Tenninkyo Gorge, is now inaccessible due to a recent landslide. We are awaiting construction of a new access trail to the falls. | | | | | --- | --- | | [![Picture](https://www.hokkaidonaturetours.com/uploads/5/9/6/6/59665553/img-0052_orig.jpg)](https://www.hokkaidonaturetours.com/hnt-private-custom-made-tours-preferences-form.html) | ## Fall Sightseeing around Daisetsuzan
Daisetsuzan National Park offers great sightseeing opportunities:
- Ride the Asahidake and Kurodake ropeways
- Biei Blue Pond & Shirahige Falls
- Enjoy the charms of Hokkaido _inaka_ towns such as Higashikawa, Furano and Biei

## Japan Autumn Foliage Forecast 2026

Although Japan’s fall color forecast varies from year to year, it’s not quite as temperamental as the one for cherry blossoms. As a result, even if a warmer autumn leads to an later season or a cooler one leads to an earlier one, I’ve founded that most years are pretty similar.

When is autumn in Japan 2026? Well, the Japan Meteorological Corporation will release its first forecast in early September 2026, which will predict how peak color will be compared to a “normal” year. However, do keep in mind that forecasts aren’t generally accurate until much later in the season—take the first one with a grain of salt.

Regardless of a particular forecast, here are the approximate times you can expect to enjoy autumn colors in Japan:

| Destination | Yellow leaves | Red leaves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Daisetsuzan** | September 15 | September 25 |
| **Hachimantai** | October 5 | October 15 |
| **Mt. Hakkoda** | October 15 | October 25 |
| **Kakunodate** | October 25 | November 5 |
| **Nikko** | October 25 | November 5 |
| **Koyasan** | October 25 | November 5 |
| **Kurobe Gorge** | November 5 | November 15 |
| **Tokyo** | November 25 | December 5 |
| **Takayama** | November 5 | November 15 |
| **Fuji Five Lakes** | October 25 | November 5 |
| **Kanazawa** | November 15 | November 25 |
| **Kyoto** | November 25 | November 25 |
| **Setouchi** | November 25 | November 25 |
| **Shikoku** | November 25 | December 5 |
| **San’in** | November 25 | November 25 |
| **Kyushu** | November 25 | December 5 |

As far as how I formulate my autumn color forecasts, in 2026 and otherwise? If the months of September and October are warmer than average, I expect autumn colors to appear later than usual. The inverse is also true: In colder years, autumn colors come to Japan sooner. Other factors can also delay the colors or bring them forward, mostly notably rainfall (or lack thereof)

In order to monitor this for yourself, keep an eye on temperatures in the cities or prefectures where you want to enjoy fall foliage, and compare them to the averages you find posted online. You can also check “Recent” pictures of your target destinations on Instagram, although you should make sure they were recently taken, and not just recently posted.

## Best Places to See Autumn Leaves in Japan in 2026

### Kyoto

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Daigo-ji.jpg)

As is the case during the spring with the _sakura_, Kyoto is one of the most satisfying places in Japan to see autumn colors, no matter what the [Kyoto autumn](https://japanstartshere.com/2023/09/13/where-can-you-see-fall-colors-in-kyoto/) leaves forecast 2026 ends up holding. My favorite places in Kyoto to see autumn colors include **Arashiyama** ( **Tenryu-ji** temple, **Okochi Sanso Villa** and the entire shoreline of the **Katsuura River**) as well as **Higashiyama** temples like **Nanzen-ji** and **Kiyomizu-dera**, and more distant temples such as **Daigo-ji** and **Kurama-dera**. There are also many awesome [Kyoto autumn color](https://japanstartshere.com/2018/12/03/autumn-in-kyoto/) spots on the periphery of the city, from **Tofuku-ji** along the **Nara Line** en route to **Fushimi** district, to **Kurama-dera** north of the center.

### Tokyo

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/Tokyo-Autumn.jpg)

Now, I’d like to tell you where you can go in Tokyo to enjoy autumn for yourself, whether for Tokyo autumn 2026 or another year. Obviously, the most famous [autumn color spot in Tokyo](https://japanstartshere.com/2023/12/12/see-autumn-leaves-in-tokyo/) is **Meiji Jingu Gaien**, aka **Ginkgo Avenue**, but that’s not the only game in town. In particular, I love **Koishikawa Koraku-en** and **Rikugi-en** gardens within the city limits; **Yokohama**‘s **Sankei-en** garden is also very worth a visit, if you have time during your fall 2026 Japan trip. Additionally, as you can see above, colorful trees (especially yellow ginkgos) are strewn throughout the heart of the city, including in **Marunouchi** just west of **Tokyo Station**.

_NOTE: Tokyo is obviously also a great base for day trips to Japan autumn destinations, including **[Hakone](https://japanstartshere.com/2025/12/22/hakone-in-autumn/)** and **Kamakura**. **Nikko**, too, although that one deserves its own section, which you will find below._

### Mt. Fuji

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Mt-Fuji-Autumn.jpg)

The autumn forecast Japan 2026 can be vague for areas around [**Mt. Fuji**](https://japanstartshere.com/mt-fuji-travel-guide/), since they differ so much in terms of elevation and other climactic conditions. For instance, while it’s possible to see autumn colors in coastal **Shizuoka** prefecture and even along the shores of **Lake Kawaguchi** and **Lake Yamanaka** well into the end of November, you’ll want to visit earlier in the month (or maybe even October) if hiking trails closer to Japan’s most famous mountain are [where you want to see Fuji’s autumn colors](https://japanstartshere.com/2025/12/19/mt-fuji-in-autumn/). Early November, meanwhile, is usually the best time to get the “money shot” behind **Chureito Pagoda** in **Fujiyoshida**.

### Hokuriku

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Eihei-ji-Autumn.jpg)

Irrespective of whether you plan to visit during autumn Japan 2026 or another year, **[Hokuriku](https://japanstartshere.com/2025/12/22/hokuriku-in-autumn/)** is one of my favorite places in Japan to enjoy autumn colors. The obvious choice here is **[Kanazawa](https://japanstartshere.com/2025/05/07/things-to-do-in-kanazawa/)** and its famed **Kenroku-en** garden, though I wouldn’t sleep on neighboring areas, be that **Nata-dera** temple in **Komatsu** (which, like Kanazawa, is in **Ishikawa**), or Eihei-ji temple in **Fukui** or **Kurobe Gorge** in **Toyama**. As a general rule, colors further from the sea and higher in elevation will change first, with red leaves reaching their peak as early as the first week of November and as late as the first week of December.

### The Japanese Alps

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Takayama-Autumn.jpg)

Whether in Fukui, Kanazawa or Toyama, Hokuriku is just a stone’s throw from the **[Japanese Alps](https://japanstartshere.com/2025/12/19/japanese-alps-in-autumn/)**, which are bounded by Nagano on the other side. If you’re coming to this region during the month of October, you might want to visit the **Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route** near **Toyama** or **Kamikochi Valley** near **Matsumoto**. In November, on the other hand, autumn colors along the historical [**Nakasendo Trail**](https://japanstartshere.com/2022/11/30/nakasendo-trail-guide/) will be nearing their peak, as will those in **Shirakawago** and **Takayama**. You could also visit the somewhat understated **Monet’s Pond** in **Gifu** prefecture, though in this case I recommend going in the very early morning to avoid crowds

### Koyasan

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Koyasan-Autumn.jpeg)

**Wakayama** prefecture’s **[Mt. Koya](https://japanstartshere.com/2023/02/21/koyasan-temple-stay/)** is a somewhat evergreen destination (and not just because of all the evergreen trees atop it), but especially shines in the autumn, when [colors usually peak in early-to-mid November](https://japanstartshere.com/2025/12/19/koyasan-in-autumn/). While colors are at their most dramatic at the **Danjo Garan** sacred complex and in **Koyasan Town**, there are a surprising number of red maples and yellow ginkgoes in **Okuno-in** cemetery, in spite of it being typically defined by its iconic cedar trees.

### Nikko

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/Nikko-Autumn.jpg)

I can understand why **Nikko**, a histor city in **Tochigi** prefecture just north of Tokyo, might seem like an afterthought for your Japan autumn 2026 trip. Most people come to this place, which centers around 17th-century **Tosho-gu** shrine as a day trip from Tokyo, assuming they come at all. This is complicated in autumn, at least if you’re not careful: While Tokyo’s leaves tend to change around or just before December 1, Nikko’s (particularly those near **Kegon Falls** and **Lake Chuzenji**) often turn yellow, orange and red a full month (or even six weeks!) earlier.

### Hokkaido

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/Hokkaido-Blue-Pond.jpeg)

Another place to go if you’ll only have time to visit Japan during the earlier part of the season? **[Hokkaido](https://japanstartshere.com/2023/10/31/hokkaido-autumn-itinerary/)** [autumn](https://japanstartshere.com/2023/10/31/hokkaido-autumn-itinerary/) 2026 may be your best bet for seeing leaves! For visits in early-to-mid October you’ll want to head east from **Sapporo**, whether to the **[Shirogane Blue Pond](https://japanstartshere.com/2023/10/31/how-to-visit-shirogane-blue-pond/)** in **Biei** near **Asahikawa**, or even over to **Sounkyo Onsen** or up to **Mt. Daisetsuzan**.

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Hakodate-Autumn.jpg)

Or to the wild **Shiretoko Peninsula**, be it to the inland lakes of **Kussharo**, **Mashu** and **Akan**, or past the town of **Utoro** toward the **Shiretoko Five Lakes** marsh. If you’re visiting in late October or early November, meanwhile, this is when Sapporo-adjacent autumn spots such as the _onsen_ towns of **Jozankei** and **Noboribetsu** will see their colors change; underrated **[Hakodate](https://japanstartshere.com/2025/02/17/things-to-do-in-hakodate/)** will also peak at this time.

### Tohoku

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Lake-Towada-Autumn-1.jpg)

Japan’s superlative **[Tohoku](https://japanstartshere.com/tohoku-travel-guide/)** region, meanwhile, sees leaves change a bit later than Hokkaido—which is to say, in line with when many places in North America and Europe experience autumn. If you’re planning an October or early November autumn trip to Japan, therefore, it makes sense to visit the northern half-dozen prefectures of Honshu island.

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/Kakunodate-6.jpg)

Some of my personal favorite spots in these regions for autumn colors include **[Lake Towada](https://japanstartshere.com/2025/12/29/lake-towada/)** and **Oirase Stream**, both in **[Aomori](https://japanstartshere.com/aomori-travel-guide/)** prefecture, as well as **[Yamadera](https://japanstartshere.com/2022/12/08/yamadera-day-trip/)** temple in **Yamagata** and **Ouchi-juku** village in **[Fukushima](https://japanstartshere.com/2022/11/30/is-fukushima-worth-visiting/)**. I also love the autumn colors in **[Kakunodate](https://japanstartshere.com/2022/10/05/is-kakunodate-worth-visiting/)** _Samurai_ village, at **Geibikei** gorge and in **[Hiraizumi](https://japanstartshere.com/2024/05/06/is-hiraizumi-worth-visiting/)**, aka the “Kyoto of the North.”

### Setouchi

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Bitchu-Matsuyama-Castle-1.jpg)

I feel like the **Seto Inland Sea** is not among the top destinations people search when consulting the Japan autumn leaves forecast 2026. But it should be. Foliage in **[Setouchi](https://japanstartshere.com/setouchi-travel-guide/)** is magnificent even in the major cities of the region: In **[Hiroshima](https://japanstartshere.com/hiroshima-travel-guide/)** near the **A-Bomb Dome**; at **Okayama**‘s **Korakuen** garden; and in **Ritsurin**, **Takamatsu**‘s treasure. Obviously, this beauty is even more pronounced the more off the beaten path you go, be that to **Bitchu Matsuyama**‘s “castle in the clouds,” to deer-filled **[Miyajima](https://japanstartshere.com/2022/12/08/is-miyajima-worth-visiting/)** island or to the harbor city of **[Onomichi](https://japanstartshere.com/2022/12/05/is-onomichi-worth-visiting/)**, whose **Old Temple Trail** is arguably at its most enchanting during the autumn.

### San’in

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/Sanin-Japan.jpg)

Heading to the other coast of far-western Honshu island takes up to **[San’in](https://japanstartshere.com/2024/04/10/sanin-itinerary/)**, which is in general one of my favorite regions of Japan. Autumn colors here are pretty “late” in general, usually peaking around early December in the castle city of **[Matsue](https://japanstartshere.com/2024/12/25/is-matsue-worth-visiting/)**, at **[Izumo Shrine](https://japanstartshere.com/2024/12/25/how-to-visit-izumo-shrine/)** and in underrated Yonago, though certain destinations (towering **Mt. Daisen**; inland **[Nageirei-do](https://japanstartshere.com/2023/03/06/nageiredo-temple-hike/)** temple) can see their colors peak in November. No matter when you come, however, you’re guaranteed a relatively tranquil and tourist-free _momijigari_ experience.

### Iya Valley

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Iya-Valley-Autumn.jpg)

I briefly mentioned **[Shikoku](https://japanstartshere.com/shikoku-travel-guide/)** autumn colors earlier in the context of the **Seto Inland Sea**, but I wanted to call particular attention to those in the inland **[Iya Valley](https://japanstartshere.com/2023/08/27/iya-valley-itinerary/)**. There are a couple of advantages to going here, and not just because of how much the wild scenery suits the blazing leaves of fall in Japan. For starters, whether at **Oboke Gorge** or near the **Kazurabashi Vine Bridge**, peak season here tends to be in mid-to-late November, several weeks earlier than in Shikoku’s cities. This can make an excursion here worthwhile even if you can’t stay into December, which is when most leaves in southern Japan are at their most brilliant.

## When Does Japan’s Autumn Foliage Usually Peak?

Whether we’re talking about autumn foliage Japan 2026 or in general, autumn leaves in Japan follow a rather predictable pattern. Specifically, you can expect to see peak _koyo_ color according to the following calendar:

- **Late September:** Hokkaido and high-altitude [Tohoku autumn](https://japanstartshere.com/2025/12/19/tohoku-in-autumn/) destinations
- **Early-to-Mid October:** Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route; Tohoku’s Aomori prefecture
- **Late October to Early November:** The rest of Tohoku; the [Japanese Alps](https://japanstartshere.com/japanese-alps-itinerary/); Fuji Five Lakes; [Nikko](https://japanstartshere.com/2022/11/23/how-many-days-in-nikko/); [Mt. Koya](https://japanstartshere.com/2018/06/11/koyasan-temple-stay/)
- **Mid-to-Late November:** [Kanazawa](https://japanstartshere.com/kanazawa-travel-guide/); [Kansai](https://japanstartshere.com/kyoto-osaka-itinerary/); Setouchi; most of Shikoku; most of [Kyushu](https://japanstartshere.com/kyushu-travel-guide/); [San’in](https://japanstartshere.com/japan-off-the-beaten-path/)
- **Early December:** [Tokyo](https://japanstartshere.com/places-to-visit-in-tokyo/) and southern Kyushu, plus [Shikoku](https://japanstartshere.com/shikoku-travel-guide/)

You should note that these dates represent the peak of colors for all trees, whether for autumn in Japan 2026 or a different year. Japanese authorities also release a so-called “yellow leaves” forecast, which predicts when Japan’s famous ginkgo trees will change colors.

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Shirakawago-Autumn.jpg)

## Is it Too Early to Plan a Japan Autumn Itinerary?

Autumn in Japan 2026 will start when the hillsides of Daisetsuzan National Park blaze red and orange in late September or early October. Accommodation for major Japan autumn leaves destinations will quickly fill up for 2026, so I’d recommend booking your hotels and ryokan as soon as possible.

## Other FAQ About Autumn in Japan 2026

### What months are autumn in Japan 2026?

Japan’s autumn colors begin in Hokkaido in late September, color the hillsides of Tohoku and the Japanese Alps from mid-October through mid-November, and reach their peak in Kyoto, Hiroshima and eventually Tokyo as November gives way to December.

### Where should I go in Japan in autumn?

As I mentioned in the beginning of this article, you can find autumn beauty throughout Japan, from rural hillsides and gorges in Hokkaido and the Tohoku regions, to ancient historical districts from Kyoto’s Higashiyama ward to the town of Takayama in the Japanese Alps.

### Is it cold in autumn in Japan?

Japan can be downright hot at the official beginning of autumn in late September, with temperatures in major cities well above 25ºC or 80ºF. However, by the times leaves change wherever you choose to see them, things will have cooled down substantially. You can expect crisp days with temperatures around 10ºC, and chilly nights approaching (or sometimes dipping below) freezing.

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Japan-Autumn-Night.jpg)

## The Bottom Line

Whether it’s six months or just six weeks away by the time you read this, autumn in Japan 2026 is closer than you think—the time to start planning is now! Split a week or two in late November between Tokyo and Kyoto, or come earlier in the season and visit somewhere more non-traditional, be that in off-the-beaten path Tohoku or in the scenic Fuji Five Lakes region. One thing to note about Japan fall foliage 2026, if you’re feeling stressed, is that they’re much less fickle than the [cherry blossoms](https://japanstartshere.com/cherry-blossom-season-japan/)—they last longer, too. Still, if you’re feeling uneasy about planning your trip or simply don’t have time to do it, there’s another option.
